anna.li: Quick sync — spotted a perf regression when running fused-attn + tensor/pipeline-parallel on 8xA100. p99 latency +25%, throughput -18% for seq=1024.

jia.wu: Did you repro on both FP16 and INT8 quant modes?

anna.li: Repro on FP16. INT8 not tried yet. Key detail: runtime picked non-fused attention kernel for TP shards because QKV layout didn't match expected stride.

mike.ram: Snapshot from the profiler (nsight):
```
GPU 0: compute 46.2ms, all-reduce 28.9ms, idle gaps 8.1ms
GPU 1..7: similar pattern, NCCL all-reduce across 8 ranks dominating at tail.
Kernel version: fused_attention_v2 skipped -> fallback to attention_split_qkv_v1
```

sanjay.k: That fallback explains it. Fused attention saves a lot for big seqs but only if QKV are all-gathered in the right shape. TP layout + our QKV sharding produced 3 separate small all-gathers instead of one batched gather.

jia.wu: Also saw KV cache scatter on decode causing extra cross-rank comms per step. KV layout in cache is (tp_shard, head, seq, dim_per_head) and our scatter was doing per-head all-gather instead of grouping by seq.

perf-bot: automatic-alert: regression >15% detected for job run/2026-07-01-26. Tagging @eng-runtime.

mike.ram: Quick config we used: 
```yaml
serving:
  model_name: llama-70b
  tp: 8
  pipeline: 1
  fused_attention: auto  # runtime decides
  qkv_strategy: all_gather_qkv  # intended
  kv_cache_layout: [tp_shard, head, seq, head_dim]
```

anna.li: Runtime kernel-selection heuristic currently checks: seq_len, head_dim mod 64, contiguous QKV buffer flag. But when TP interleaves shards the contiguous flag is false and it picks split kernels. We need a path to reshape+coalesce QKV to allow fused kernel.

jia.wu: Another edge: flash-attn triggers OOM on certain seq lengths that are multiples of 128 with our current block-size heuristic. It falls back to non-flash, which is slower and increases memory churn leading to extra cudaMallocs between tokens.

mike.ram: Profiling trace shows NCCL ops are not fully overlapped: all-reduce launched on default stream, fused-attn compute on per-GPU stream; but no explicit comm/compute overlap because tensor cores are saturating one stream and NCCL kernels wait. We can try enqueue NCCL on a high-priority stream and use cudaGraph for capture.

sanjay.k: Actionable next steps I propose:
- Add a runtime pass to detect TP QKV layout and rewrite QKV to fused layout before kernel selection (cheap reshape/copy if needed).
- Improve batching heuristic: prefer slightly larger minibatches to amortize all-reduce latency for small token updates.
- Implement async NCCL progress + overlap primitives around KV all-gather so decode-step comm overlaps with next-token compute.
- Add an avoid-flash fallback for sequences that trigger worst-case memory pattern (detect seq % 128 == 0 as a heuristic).

anna.li: Agreed. Also add telemetry: log kernel-choice reason (why fused skipped) and per-step all-reduce size+latency to pinpoint scatter/gather frequency.

jia.wu: I'll prototype a QKV coalesce shim that does: 
```python
# pseudo
if tp_sharded_qkv and not contiguous:
    qkv = qkv.reshape(batch, heads, 3, seq, head_dim)
    qkv = qkv.transpose(2,0,1,3,4).contiguous()
    # single all-gather on axis=0
```
Should be cheap if we can reuse pinned staging buffer across batches.

mike.ram: I'll run large-scale repro with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO and capture traces for 8 runs to compare before/after.

perf-bot: run-status: job 2026-07-01-26 requeued with perf tags.

anna.li: Great. Let's keep this thread for updates. If anyone sees a quick win (kernel override flag or small QKV reorder) drop a PR and ping here. :thumbsup:
